client_brief:
A restrained Balance Brief excerpt with consistent presenter covers

Vitale Labs' positioning is restraint. The Balance Brief should earn trust through clear, approved content, not add dramatic wellness promises. This commission uses six short clips for an edit of twenty-one seconds or less, with matching cover and portrait preparations.

A deliberate 21-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 6 supplied short clips using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. Source time ranges must come from motion_source_metadata.json and a task-specific edit decision list. The supplied video files contain no audio streams; use a separate supplied WAV only where one exists and never infer dialogue from silent footage.

Three episode covers at feed size brought to one series look, one white point, one warmth, one crop logic and the presenter at one height in frame across three different filming mornings, with a confined correction where a global move fails, plus the per episode portrait variant on the house ground that the printed card binds. No cover carries another company's packaging and no cover reaches its size by enlargement. Per frame parameter log included, with one line on why each morning differs from its neighbours.

Please keep Dr. Nadia Reuter at a consistent scale across the three covers, despite the different filming mornings. Where a global colour adjustment fails, make a confined correction. No cover should contain another company's packaging or reach its size through enlargement.

Supplied materials: source_video_files/ (6 measured short files); motion_source_metadata.json; balance_brief_stills/ (9 on set stills, 3 per morning, camera scale); balance_card_2025.pdf; balance_captions.txt.

Media inventory: 6 video files, 30.252 seconds in total; 0 with embedded audio; 0 separate audio files (0 seconds). These measured sources set the production limits.

The video files are silent. A separate supplied WAV may be used where available, but neither the visuals nor an automated selection establish a medical claim or dialogue. Stay with the approved material and record the real source timings.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the final edit decision list and measured source metadata. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem. Keep runtime within measured source duration and the stated cap; do not invent footage or dialogue.

The commission is budgeted at $2,500-$6,500 fixed. We have allowed 2 to 4 weeks, including one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com short form video post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, seeking an editor for a health, wellness and genetics channel wanting 'educational, engaging, social-media driven' Reels and Shorts from a presenter who films long straight to camera takes, with the ideal freelancer explicitly comfortable with 'pacing, and social-media style'. The real company and presenter are laundered to the coined, IP clean brand Vitale Labs, its mini series The Balance Brief, and the presenter persona Dr. Nadia Reuter; no real brand, product, person or trademark is named. REPOSITIONED for connector reality, as the ledger's own note concedes: the literal post implies open timeline Premiere and After Effects work (multi track compositing, motion graphics, burned in captions, trim to timestamp assembly), none of which this connector performs. The honest fuller commission that same client genuinely needed is the whole drop rather than the timeline: automatic highlight cutting and same source reframing for the cuts, a speech pass judged across the set rather than per file, three mornings of on set stills brought to one cover look, the clinic partner episode card rebuilt from the press artwork as a real record per page run, and the on screen wording handed back as a working file the client edits when the air dates move. That is a posted job of the same shape and the same money, made producible.

price_band_and_audience: A forty dollar monthly subscription supplement bought by a wellness curious thirty to fifty year old who has been burned by overclaiming. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push it up into near black grounds, cold hard light, a slow authored title sequence and a whispered voice and it becomes a two hundred dollar longevity clinic, which misprices a forty dollar bottle and reads as a claim the reviewer never cleared. Push it down into saturated fast cuts, shouted supers, a bright bounce grade and stacked benefit captions and it becomes a discount aisle stack of gummies, which in this category reads as hype and is precisely what makes a cautious buyer close the tab. The correct answer sits between them: daylight in a real lab, unhurried pacing, a warm neutral rather than a clinical blue, restrained type, and one cleared sentence given room rather than six claims crammed in. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even where every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 dollars fixed for the drop.

brand_identity.sector: Direct to consumer supplement line sold on subscription, with a short form educational video series.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2018, Denver, Colorado, a small direct to consumer supplement company with an in house presenter.
brand_identity.about: Vitale Labs is a small Denver supplement line sold direct to consumers on subscription. Its presenter, Dr. Nadia Reuter, fronts a short explainer series, The Balance Brief, that turns one cleared claim per episode into a calm, credible watch. The brand's whole positioning is restraint: it speaks to buyers who have been burned by overclaiming, and it rewards being believed over being loud.
brand_identity.audience: Wellness curious buyers aged 30 to 50, cautious about health claims and burned by overclaiming before. They reward evidence and plain speech, and they close the tab on hype.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Bottles around 40 dollars a month on subscription. Positioned between a discount gummy stack and a 200 dollar longevity clinic: credible and warm, never clinical and never hyped.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a warm, humanist serif that reads as considered rather than clinical. Text: a clean humanist sans, generous and unhurried. One cleared sentence is given room rather than six claims crammed in. Nothing cold and nothing shouted.
brand_identity.voice: Measured, warm and plain. States what is known and stops there. Example line: 'One change, explained clearly. No promises we cannot keep.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The brand runs on the artwork its printer used last season. The episode card exists as the press PDF the printer worked from, and the per episode details live in a supplied sheet. Type and colour direction are inherited from that card rather than from a formal guideline, and the regulatory reviewer's cleared claim lines are fixed and cannot be reworded.
brand_identity.values: Credibility over reach: never a claim the reviewer did not clear.

assets_supplied.name: balance_brief_stills/ (9 on set stills, 3 per morning, camera scale)
assets_supplied.kind: Stills the photographer shot alongside each filming morning, three per episode, natural window light on two mornings and a panel on the third.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The covers come from these. Three per morning. Put them together and they do not look like one series yet, and one morning we shared the bench with a supplier."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The panel lit morning renders the presenter's white lab coat with a cast that a single warm correction across the set turns green rather than neutral, so that morning needs a confined correction the other two do not. Separately the only frame from that morning with usable expression carries a supplier's carton at the right edge, which cannot be retouched out and can only be cropped away, and cropping far enough to lose it takes the frame under the cover size the feeds need, with enlargement the only way back.

assets_supplied.name: balance_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the printer used for last season's episode card, one card, a continuous block of set copy over a portrait frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card exactly as it went to press last season. Please keep the design and change only the per episode details."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Its typeset copy is one continuous flow, so it converts to a single text frame rather than the separate title, presenter and detail frames the printed page suggests, and the mapping readout for that frame silently omits one run while keeping its line break, so every offset computed past that point is short by exactly that run and the validator still returns valid. The title measure is also fixed and does not spill: a record longer than last season's simply stops rendering at trim.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which visible beats in the measured short clips actually cut together without a continuity jump, duplicate action, or missing subject.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Filenames and source duration do not establish visual continuity. The first assembled proof is the earliest reliable evidence.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Replace or reorder source ranges, shorten the piece, and rebuild the EDL around the strongest continuous action.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A technically valid render feels accidental or implies an action that the source never completes.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the approved horizontal composition survives the required vertical or square reframe with the subject and essential interface or product detail still visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The crop depends on the actual chosen ranges and subject position inside each rendered frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Choose a different source range for the platform version or use fit instead of fill and revise the surrounding design treatment.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The platform export is correctly sized but loses the person, product, or interface that gives the shot meaning.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the silent final piece still communicates clearly without implying dialogue, ambience, or music that was never supplied.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: This can be judged only on the final rendered sequence, not from a successful operation response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Strengthen visual sequencing or approved on-screen copy without fabricating a soundtrack.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The deliverable relies on absent sound and fails when viewed as supplied.
